problem: Existing safety, anomaly and embodied VLM benchmarks rely on human annotations, single-view RGB, retrospective labels or semantic danger narratives. They do not test whether a VLM can bind visual evidence to the robot's own body geometry to infer present or imminent robot-induced collision, under physically exact labels.
motivation: A VLM-based safety monitor for human-robot co-presence must decide whether the robot body is safely separated, colliding with the scene or a person, or about to collide. Standard ISO safeguards are local and reactive and do not answer this visual question. The paper calls the missing skill 'collision grounding' and probes it with simulator-derived contact labels across views and modalities.
key_idea: Build a Habitat 3.0 benchmark with simulator-derived contact labels, multi-view RGB-D and top-down maps, and use it to test whether frontier VLMs can classify current collision state and warn of imminent collision.
insight: VLMs are visually fluent but physically under-grounded. Depth variants do not monotonically help (the 'depth paradox'), so depth is not turned into robot-body contact evidence unless tied to body extent and thresholds. Robotics pretraining (Gemini Robotics-ER) lowers false alarms but not Macro-F1 (FAR_any 14.0 with Depth Color vs 60-90 for GPT-5.5). Top-down maps suppress false alarms (FAR_any 6.0) but collapse Task 1 (MF1 24.2), and robot-scene contact is the blind spot (21.5% Task 1 accuracy vs 39% for human contact).
method: Episode generation: Habitat 3.0 social navigation and social rearrangement in HSSD-HAB scenes, with 49 scenes, 10 seeds per scene-task pair, 3 SMPL-X humanoid appearances and 9 YCB objects, giving 2,940 episodes (Spot robot).
Observation space: four synchronized RGB-D streams (robot-arm ego, human-head ego, third-person robot, third-person human), a top-down trajectory map, and camera intrinsics/extrinsics.
Task 1 (Safety Event Classification): a 3-frame clip is labeled A safe (including near-miss hard negatives), B robot-scene contact or C robot-human contact, from simulator contact flags.

Task 2 (Collision Early Warning): predict imminent scene or human contact within a short horizon (30-frame pre-window for scene, offsets 5-20 frames for human). Near-miss, post-collision and easy clips are labeled no-risk.

Evaluation protocol: 450 balanced clips per task (150 per class), with Accuracy, Macro-F1, per-class F1 and FAR_C / FAR_any on near misses. Models return structured JSON with distance, trend and collision flags as diagnostics.

Stage I / II ablations: Stage I sweeps 9 ego-only representations (RGB, depth, colorized depth, predicted depth, RGB-D combinations). Stage II fixes RGB and varies ego / all-views / top-down. Both are run on GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 (frozen, prompted zero-shot)
setting.observation: 3-frame clips of ego / third-person RGB and depth (true or predicted), plus a top-down trajectory map
setting.action_space: none (classification: label A/B/C for state or risk)
setting.privileged: none for the models (labels come from simulator contact state); the simulator-depth conditions use ground-truth depth

numbers.eval_set_note: 450 balanced clips (150 per class) sampled from 2,940 episodes; all-view RGB is the best Task 1 condition

results: No model is reliable: the best Task 1 Macro-F1 is 56.2 (GPT-5.5, all-view RGB) and the best Task 2 Macro-F1 is 51.2 (Gemini 3.1 Pro, ego Depth Color). Robot-scene contact is the hardest subtype (21.5% Task 1 accuracy; 34.1% for scene-collision warning). Top-down maps cut false alarms to FAR_any 34.0 / 28.0 / 6.0 but hurt current-state recognition.
limitations: Simulation only, with fixed Habitat tasks and 3 humanoid appearances, evaluating short clips with no closed-loop intervention or real-world validation.
Scene-collision samples come only from social navigation, and human collisions are terminal in the simulator, which creates an asymmetry in subtype interpretation.
Only prompted frontier VLMs are evaluated, with no explicit-geometry or trained baselines, so the diagnosis is not yet paired with a fix.
